page.layout: Top: running head with page number at left. Two circular portrait medallions side by side, each with its inscription around the rim. Below them one block of text in two entries, the first beginning "LVDOVICA", the second "MARGARETA". No margin notes, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.p: LVDOVICA Exclarissima Sabaudię Ducũ familia,illu-strissimo Angolismorũ Duci nupsit:cui & duo præcipua nostrę ætatis lumina peperit, Francifcũ Valesiũ, quipost Ludouici 12. mortem Gallici regni habenas tenuit,& Margaretā postea Hē-rici inclyti Nauarrę Regis vxorem. Hęc tanto ingenio mulier, tantáque in arduis rebus obeũdis dexteritate fuit, vt nō immerito filius loginquiore expeditione suscepta,regni totius administrationem amplissima cũ potestate ei semper crediderit. Ex præclarissimis eius in rem Christianam promeritis, illud præcipuè memoria dignum est,quòd anno 1529. mense Augusto, initio Cameraci cũ Margareta Maximiliani filia colloquio,pacem stabilierit,liberósque regios, Francifcum Delphinũ, & Hēricũ Aurelianorum id temporis Ducem, paternorum pastorum in Hispania obsides,paretis patrięque desiderio restituerit.Supremum diem claufit 11. Cal.Octob. anno 1531. singularis quandiu vixit,ingeniorum & virtutis fautrix. Vide Chr. Cari. & Galliæ,.

MARGARETA Austriaca,Maximiliani Cęsaris,& Mariæ Burgundæ filia, anno salutis nostræ 1479. vitæ limen ingressa est.Nupsit primùm Georgio Hispaniarũ Principi, eóque è viuis sublato, Philiberto Allobrogum Duci, quo præmaturè orbata,cũ in cœlibatu persisteret,nomine Caroli quinti, fratris sui filij,Flandrię Germanięque inferioris gubernacula suscepit. Anno deinde 1529. habito Cameraci cum Ludouica Francifci Regis matre colloquio,compositis Principum cõtrouersiis, lætam suis pacem peperit:annóque in sequenti magno suorũ desiderio factis concefsit. Vide Genealog. Carol. quinti.

page.notes: No marginal notes. Two circular woodcut medallions above the text carry the inscriptions transcribed above. The medallion inscriptions were read from the rim and may be partly damaged. The "12" after Ludouici is read from the old-style numeral. Long s has been written as plain s throughout, per the rules.
